kind: AI software correction following historical AI software review
finding_fixed: AI-01-F1 and the same SQLite integer overflow in notice-ID handlers
exact_changes: Add SQLite signed-64-bit maximum constant. load_notice now rejects IDs outside 1..9223372036854775807 with 404 before SQL binding, covering detail, photo, edit, returned and admin removal handlers.
Reject positive browse pages greater than 1152921504606846976 with HTTP 400 before computing a SQLite OFFSET. The maximum safe page and ordinary empty pages retain HTTP 200 behavior.
Catch ValueError when converting digit-like category strings, and reject category integers above 9223372036854775807 with HTTP 400. Valid category values continue to filter normally.
Keep existing negative/invalid page fallback to page 1 and ignored nonnumeric/negative browse categories. Do not clamp invalid numeric IDs into existing rows.
Leave category form validation unchanged: real create/edit probes establish that oversized positive/negative strings already render the existing inline validation error without writes.
Add four regression methods covering integer boundaries, all seven notice-route method combinations, no unintended notice writes, valid filtered pagination and safe existing fallback behavior.

red.explanation: Six browse cases returned 500 instead of 400; fourteen notice-ID route cases returned 500 instead of 404. Valid-pagination and form-rejection characterization methods passed before the fix.

tdd.note: Two additional existing-fallback controls (5,000-digit positive page and negative category) were added after the initial red run and before the implementation; the regression method count remained four.

suite_execution_note: Executed every command from TESTS.bat with portable Python -B, avoiding only its interactive pause. Full test_app execution is logged separately and not repeated in the remaining-suite loop.

historical_baseline.note: The original 15-test AI-01 review remains historical and still describes the pre-fix snapshot.

limitations: No browser or human usability study was conducted.
This verification uses local automated tests and synthetic temporary fixtures; it does not claim human participation.
No Canva or report documents were changed. No persistent participant records were created.
